image.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: high-fidelity desktop application screenshot used as a UI implementation reference. Input image: reference only, the actual current TabPlayer Windows music notation editor; preserve its established practical compact workstation style and overall panes. Generate ONE new screenshot extending only its Backing synchronization workflow. This is a Rust/Tauri professional cross-platform notation/tab editor. Flat charcoal #23272f panels, near-black plot, fine slate borders, compact 12–14px system sans text, restrained pale blue active states, cream music notation paper with black guitar notation and six-string TAB. No new branding, gradients, glow, cards, decorative texture, marketing or glass. Full app screenshot approximately1600x1000. Top menu/document-tabs/transport, narrow left Backing controls, wide central score, right Inspector remain recognizable as reference. Preserve existing gain/pan and numeric anchor controls, right Inspector width and practical score area. Bottom dock ends before right Inspector; tabs Overview, Mixer, Instrument, Backing with Backing active.
New purpose: synchronize written music to a prerecorded audio performance without stretching the reference. Left Backing sidebar keeps existing filename/import/offset/gain/pan/mute/solo controls; a compact expanded 'Sync timing' section contains a select labeled 'Timing' with selected value 'Score follows audio', then clearly paired numeric fields 'Entry (ms)' value1000 and 'Exit (ms)' value7000. Use concise real desktop inputs, not cards. A short muted label 'Reference audio stays linear' explains this mode. Compact two secondary actions 'From score' with dropdown indicator and 'Write score tempos'. No onboarding paragraph or modal.
The Backing bottom dock remains compact and internally usable. Header has source filename 'Harbour rhythm.wav', zoom minus/100%/plus/Fit aligned left, and a small timing label 'Score follows audio' toward the right. Show seconds ruler from0:00 to0:08 and subdued realistic violet stereo waveform data on dark plot. Draw a clear nondestructive playable zone from1.0s to7.0s: faintly dim the waveform before/after, distinct small inward-facing ENTRY and EXIT bracket handles at zone ends, fine blue vertical boundary lines and subtle horizontal bracket span along top edge. Two interior sync handles appear as smaller blue numbered squares visually distinct from endpoint brackets. Show a musical-grid ruler aligned to audio across this zone and two small legible segment-tempo labels '120 BPM' then '60 BPM'. A thin cream selected-score cursor is distinct from blue editable handles. Entry bracket has an obvious white keyboard-focus outline. Footer readout 'Entry · Source1,000ms · Measure1' left, existing 'Add sync point' and 'Delete sync point' buttons right. Keep labels and buttons well separated, no overlap with ticks or waveform. The central upper score has a modest blue selected passage and a few notation measures; do not redraw it as timeline or piano roll.
Constraints: extend the established interface, do not redesign the shell. New content is only sync timing, nondestructive endpoint brackets, segment-tempo readout and two conversion actions. Do not add audio pitch/filtering, trim/export actions, recording, extra tracks, meters, chat or invented features. Treat score/time values and waveform as illustrative. Output only the polished usable app screenshot.
image.review: Root inspected the actual generated pixels before P16 product work. Adopt existing charcoal/cream/blue workstation, Sync timing disclosure in Backing sidebar, explicit Timing select, paired entry/exit source-ms controls, concise mode explanation and From score/Write score tempos actions. Add waveform entry/exit brackets with distinct focused boundaries, interior sync handles and unobtrusive segment BPM readouts, dim source beyond active span. Preserve existing adaptive dock geometry ending before Inspector, numeric anchor/gain units and all unrelated shell. Actual tempo/grid/offset/occurrence relationships use contract/runtime data; image labels and larger example panes are illustrative. Existing two-channel audio must remain two real lanes even though generated stereo depiction blends lanes.
